doc.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How Paul Bley noticed her and made her write
summary: He bought cigarettes from her after she shushed customers during solos; she could not earn enough tips to return to Oakland.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So you met Paul, and you mentioned that Paul was the stimulus for you starting to write.
So you saw Paul, but how did that connection happen? What was the...
How did he know I was a musician?

Because I would never sell any cigarettes, I’d sit down there with the tray around my neck, and if someone asked me for a pack of Lucky’s I’d say “Are you crazy? Shhh! You have to be quiet until the solo’s over.”
So he said “You’re a musician.” He bought a pack of cigarettes from me and he
That’s how we met. He must have done it in the intermission, otherwise I would have yelled at him.
Some give roses and some buy a pack of cigarettes. [Laughs]

Really that’s so funny. And so he took me away from all that, because I couldn’t make enough money to go back to Oakland. I thought maybe I could go back to Oakland but I didn’t make enough money as a cigarette girl, and if I did... here’s the interesting thing... If I didn’t make enough tips, I had to make up tips out of my salary.

So I had to turn in all my tips and make up, so I had to get tips it was really weird. And that club that was, I forget who owned it, but I think it was Oscar Goodstein and, Mom... it starts with an M, Maury? No... Maury... another gangster. But I don’t know what his name was.
